title: PAR-CIM: A Precise/Approximate Reconfigurable Digital CIM Macro with 0.35-4b Fractional Mixed-Bitwidth Quantization
problem: Digital CIM for DNN acceleration faces overhead from resource usage, energy efficiency, and limited architectural flexibility in balancing precision and approximation.
motivation: Existing DCIM solutions handle approximate or reconfigurable paradigms separately; a unified design balancing precision, approximation, and flexibility is needed.
method: PAR-CIM integrates layer/gate-level approximate computation (LGAC) into adder trees achieving 0.35× area, develops fractional mixed-bitwidth quantization (FMBQ) combining Taylor sensitivity analysis with DoReFa-Net, and implements multi-bit reconfigurable computation mode (MBRM).
key_novelty: Holistic reconfigurable CIM macro combining precise and approximate computation with fractional mixed-bitwidth quantization.
limitations: Tested on ResNet18 and custom model on CIFAR-10; scalability to larger networks and datasets not demonstrated.
